title: precision-noise-playground-notes
content:
Objective:
Quick, informal investigative log for the odd NaN/quality regressions we've been seeing when enabling mixed precision on customer load (INT8/FP8 experiments). This is a scratchpad — messy steps, commands, outputs, and hypotheses. Use to reproduce and to hand off to SRE/infra if needed.

Symptoms observed:
- Intermittent NaNs in logits on ~0.5% of requests when model run with FP8 kernels + int8 activation quantization. Mostly appears under longer contexts (seq_len >= 1024) and when KV cache reused across multiple requests.
- Downstream: token sampling fails (softmax gets NaN), client sees truncated stream and hallucinated tokens once recovery kicks in.
- Correlation: higher batch sizes (>=8) and concurrent requests increase frequency.

Recent quick timeline:
- 2024-07-30: First customer report (prod) — transient 502s, logs had 'output NaN' markers.
- 2024-08-02: Canary run with debug flags --> reproduced locally with seed variant.
- 2024-08-10: Reproduced with fp8 kernels disabled = 0 NaNs. Re-enable = back to ~0.4%

Commands/recipes I used to repro locally (conda env: rwinf-quant):
- minimal run that showed NaN:
  python -m rwinf.inference.run_demo \n    --model workbench/llama-ish:chtv2 \n    --dtype fp8_e4m3 \n    --activation-quant int8 \n    --seq-len 1536 \n    --batch-size 8 \n    --use-kv-cache true \n    --seed 42 \n    --debug-nan-dump /tmp/nandump

- kernel toggle (runtime flags):
  RW_RUNTIME_DISABLE_KERNELS=attn_fused_fp8,matmul_fast_fp8 python ...

- layernorm eps test (to see sensitivity):
  export LAYERNORM_EPS=1e-6  # default 1e-5 -> lowered produced more NaNs.
  export LAYERNORM_EPS=1e-4  # higher reduced NaNs in quick runs.

Captured error snippet (truncated) from /tmp/nandump/log-2024-08-02.txt:
  2024-08-02 14:13:07,502 ERROR inference.runner: forward pass produced NaN in logits at layer 28 (attention_out)
  Traceback (most recent call last):
    File "/opt/rwinf/serving/runtime/runner.py", line 411, in forward_batch
      out = module.forward(inputs)
  RuntimeError: NaN encountered during tensor cuda op (aten::softmax)

Quick inspect of intermediate stats (printed by instrumentation hooks):
- layer 27 pre-attn stddev: 0.00012 (very low)
- layer 28 attention scores max: 1.2e6  (suspiciously large)
- attention softmax denominator had values inf/NaN after float->fp8->int8 roundtrip in scaled-softmax path

What I tried and immediate observations:
1) Disable fp8 kernels for matmuls & fused-attn:
   - result: NaNs go away, throughput down ~15% but stable.
2) Increase layernorm eps to 1e-3 globally:
   - result: NaNs drop to ~0.01% but generation slightly noisier (perp up ~0.6).
3) Clamp attention logits before softmax (hard clamp at 1e4):
   - result: stops infs but sometimes clips true high-att scores; seemed to reduce perplexity hit vs layernorm change.
4) Turn off activation-int8 quant for only attention (keep MLP int8):
   - result: NaNs drop substantially; suggests attention quant path is fragile.
5) Seed/PRNG noise test: multiple runs with seeds 1..10 showed non-deterministic bursts — not pure seed issue.
6) KV cache reuse toggle: when kv cache cleared every request, NaNs go away; suggests accumulation/scale of cached keys/values might overflow in quantized representation.

Hypotheses (ranked):
- H1: Quantized KV accumulation overflow / insufficient scale reset. FP8/int8 mix doesn't preserve dynamic range across many time steps => attention dot-products blow up.
- H2: LayerNorm numeric sensitivity — lower eps (we had micro-optimizations to lower eps earlier) caused tiny denominators after quant noise => extreme attention scores.
- H3: Fused attention kernel has a bug in fp8->int8 cast path (edge-case for long contexts).
- H4: BFloat16 fallback mixed in some layers due to kernel selection mismatch, resulting in inconsistent scaling assumptions.

Micro-probes to collect next:
- Add counters on KV magnitudes per timestep (max, mean, sign-change count) across cache reuse cycles.
- Histogram of attention dot-product values pre-softmax for layers 24-30, compare full-precision vs fp8/int8 runs.
- Trace kernel selection log per op (so we can reproduce exact kernel chain that led to NaN).

Small experiment matrix I ran (condensed):
- baseline fp32: batch8 seq1536 -> 0 NaNs (n=2000 requests)
- fp8 + int8 activations: batch8 seq1536 -> 10 NaNs (n=2000)
- fp8 + int8 + layernorm_eps=1e-3 -> 1 NaN
- fp8 + int8 + clamp_logits=1e4 -> 0 NaNs, perplexity +0.2
- int8-only (no fp8 kernels): 2 NaNs (worse than clamp)

Interpreting the matrix: clamp seems pragmatic short-term. Layernorm eps tweak is effective but modifies model numerics & may affect quality. Kernel disable is simple but costly. Need to find root cause to avoid permanent quality regressions.

Immediate mitigations to propose for rollout:
- Canary: enable hard-clamp pre-softmax in runtime for fp8/int8 combos only (config flag).
- Telemetry: instrument and log first NaN per request with kernel chain + kv magnitudes + layer id.
- Opt: force attention activation path to BF16 accumulators (even if matmul is fp8) — test for stability/perf tradeoff.

Possible long-term fixes:
- Fix: adjust fp8 scaling algorithm for KV cache accumulation (scale resets or periodic rescaling).
- Fix: add quant-stable layernorm variant (higher eps, fused with clamp) behind a flag.
- Kernel patch: audit fused-attn cast codepaths for edge cases (seq>=1024, large batch).

Notes for an automatic reproducer (what to capture to hand off):
- model config, tokenizer & seed
- exact runtime env variables (RW_RUNTIME_*) and kernel listing
- captured kernel selection log for that run
- /tmp/nandump with intermediate tensors (kv stats, dot products) at layers 20..32
- hardware: A100 80GB, CUDA 12.x, cuBLAS version X (capture exact)

One-liner debug script (quick run):
  #!/bin/bash
  export RW_RUNTIME_KERNEL_LOG=1
  export LAYERNORM_EPS=1e-5
  export RW_RUNTIME_DISABLE_KERNELS=""
  python -m rwinf.inference.run_demo --model workbench/llama-ish:chtv2 --dtype fp8_e4m3 --activation-quant int8 --seq-len 1536 --batch-size 8 --seed 42 --debug-nan-dump /tmp/nandump || true

Open questions / TODOs:
- [ ] Is the issue correlated with CUDA/cuBLAS versions? Quick matrix on 11.8 vs 12.0 needed.
- [ ] Confirm whether other models (decoder-only vs encoder-decoder) show same failure modes.
- [ ] Add test to nightly quant bisect harness that runs long-context + repeated-kv reuse workload.
- [ ] Can we add a safe-accumulate path that uses FP32 accumulators for KV but keeps output quantized?

Notes-to-self on next steps:
- Push kernel-selection logging PR (small) so we can reproduce in CI (assign to Marco).
- Prototype clamp flag in runtime and run canary on dedicated cluster (Lena to own).
- Start a short postmortem doc if we see customer-facing incidents during rollout.

Random aside (observational):
- When I artificially perturbed just one layernorm scale by +3%, NaNs disappeared in many trials — suggests fragile balance of scales across layers.

If handing off: include this doc + /tmp/nandump for one reproducible run (I've pinned one at /tmp/nandump/repro-2024-08-02.tar.gz).

End of noisy scratchpad. Will tidy into an RFC if we find deterministic repro path.
